After #37404, Mathlib.Data.Matrix.DMatrix is imported only by Mathlib.CategoryTheory.Preadditive.Mat, which is imported nowhere. That is, docs#DMatrix is used only as the type of morphisms in docs#CategoryTheory.Mat_.

In #Is there code for X? > DMatrix is a module I noted that DMatrix doesn't have either a module or multiplication structure on it. The module structure is probably pretty easy to get, but this thread suggests that DMatrix might never going to get a multiplication structure and you should basically use Mat_ instead. (I'm not so sure about this myself; maybe there could be a typeclass Mul instance if there is a family of HMul instances on the element types).

What should be the design goals of DMatrix, and when would it make sense to use it instead of a Pi type (which already has a module instance)? The main advantage of Matrix over A -> B -> R aside from making your intention clearer is that it has a multiplication, which DMatrix does not. But DMatrix does have row and column indexing operations, which could make it useful. Basically, what I would like to know is if DMatrix is "complete" or not or if there are more structures that need to be defined on it.

Also, is there any chance of Matrix being defined in terms of DMatrix, similar to the plan to define Finsupp in terms of DFinsupp?

One problem is that even if we did put a matrix structure on DMatrix is theorems about it would have hard to state hypotheses. For example, stating that multiplication in DMatrix is associative and has an identity would amount to proving that the element type is the Hom space of some category. This would be hard to put as a hypothesis.
